turns.t: Sorry, sorry, doctor, I'm late, I went to the wrong clinic, the eye one, I got halfway through the door before the receptionist stopped me. ~
No harm done, Mr Bhatt. Come in. What's the problem? ~
My thumbs. The base of both thumbs, they've been paining me. Pain at the base of the thumbs, when I grip things.
How long?
Oh, I don't know. It was before Diwali. Or after? Last year? I really can't say when it started.
Doctor, I've got the splint trolley ready, whenever you want it. ~
Thank you, Anita, in a minute. Mr Bhatt, what does it stop you doing? ~
Opening jars. Turning keys. I was a tailor for forty years, so the thumbs were my life.
Any numbness or tingling in the fingers?
No numbness. No tingling.
Any allergies, to medicines or anything else?
Hm. I think I came out in a rash once, around my eyelids, after some eye drops. But I don't remember which ones. And I'm not sure it was an allergy.
I'll note it as a possible, unconfirmed reaction. Let me take two numbers. Pulse 74, blood pressure 136 over 84.
Is that fine? ~
That's fine. Now I'd like to look at your hands. Put them flat on the table.
Like this? ~
Now press your thumb against your fingertip. ~
Ow! There. ~
I can see a bony swelling at the base of the right thumb, and it's tender when I press.
Both are like that, doctor. ~
I can see the left is a little less swollen. ~
Maybe it's the sewing. ~
Forty years of fine work will do that. ~
Shall I bring the splint, doctor? ~
Yes, please, Anita. For the night, Mr Bhatt, a thumb splint can rest the joint.
Will it hurt? ~
It's a soft one, Mr Bhatt, with velcro. Here, try it on. ~
It's very snug. ~
Good. Wear it at night and for heavy jobs. Soak your hands in warm water in the morning before you start.
In the sink? ~
Yes, a basin of warm water, five minutes. And use the large-handled tools at home, they take the strain off the thumb.
My wife bought a jar opener last week. ~
Perfect. Use it. ~
Okay, doctor. ~
Keep an eye on the pain. ~
I will. ~
I'll show you how to take the splint off, Mr Bhatt. ~
Thank you, Anita. Thank you, doctor. ~
